summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow health savings accounts (HSAs), Archer medical savings accounts (MSAs), and health flexible spending arrangements (FSAs) to be used for over-the-counter oral healthcare products, including toothbrushes, water flossers, and certain anticaries, antiplaque, or antigingivitis drug products.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands the definition of qualified medical expenses for HSAs, FSAs, and Archer MSAs to include certain oral healthcare products. This change allows individuals to use pre-tax dollars for these expenses, effectively reducing their taxable income and thus lowering their tax burden. The bill is entirely focused on this tax code amendment.

The bill expands the definition of qualified medical expenses for HSAs, Archer MSAs, FSAs, and HRAs to include OTC oral health products, allowing more spending from these tax-advantaged accounts. This increases tax expenditures and reduces federal revenue, thereby widening the deficit. The entire bill is devoted to this change.
